mechanism_of_action: Bivalent Fc-FGF21 analogue that replicates FGF21 agonism of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1c, 2c, or 3c.
primary_endpoint: Proportion with at least 1-stage fibrosis improvement and no worsening of NASH at week 24.
efficacy_outcome: In the liver biopsy analysis set, endpoint achieved by 39% (15/38) with efruxifermin 28 mg (RR 2.3, 95% CI 1.1–4.8; p=0.025) and 41% (14/34) with 50 mg (RR 2.2, 95% CI 1.0–5.0; p=0.036), versus 20% (8/41) with placebo. In the full analysis set, rates were 36% vs 19% for 28 mg (p=0.033) and 33% vs 19% for 50 mg (p=0.123).
safety_signal: Diarrhoea occurred in 40% of each efruxifermin group versus 19% with placebo; nausea in 28% and 42% versus 23%, respectively, mostly grade 1–2. Five patients discontinued due to adverse events; four serious adverse events occurred in the 50 mg group, one considered drug related; no deaths.
